tweets.nap-18060410-320: I am sorry you sent your Brother to Paris — I refused him. Tell him to rejoin at once: two millions made in Hanover buys no airs, and duty neglected over riches is disgrace. Generals leave troops at their peril.
tweets.nap-18060410-321: Start your hound pack, Eugène — Italian gentlemen must ride and hunt, not sit with their wives. The exercise will do you good. (And indulge those Irish officers who beg to march on the English in Italy — I never frown on eagerness to serve.)
tweets.nap-18060414-322: You work too hard in too grey a life — good for you, but your young wife is pregnant. Spend evenings with her, take her to company and the theatre weekly, hunt and keep hounds; I allow it in the budget. Make the house gay — my old wife asks nothing of me.
tweets.nap-18060422-323: Send Villeneuve home to Provence till his exchange. Tell Infernet I am satisfied. Bring Lucas to Paris — I shall gladly see that brave man.
tweets.nap-18060501-324: Your letters are here. Exact no oaths from priests — nothing but trouble. Go your own way; suppress the convents. Rome fumes over Lucca Concordat — ask Pius if he takes me for a weak, ignorant prince.
tweets.nap-18060510-325: Lemarois should have Ancona by now — I give him the Papal troops.
tweets.nap-18060513-326: I like your energy in governing — forty-four death and galley sentences will teach constancy. Lose no chance to humiliate Russians and English.
tweets.nap-18060516-327: I recall you from Rome — that ill-run court that torments me will be punished sooner or later. Stay while it suits, leaving politics to Alquier. Tell the Pope Consalvi note disgusts me: folly or treason, he ruins the Holy see.
tweets.nap-18060531-328: Trust Naples too much and you die poisoned — keep French cooks and French guards always. No one enters your bedroom at night but your aide-de-camp, sleeping in the next room.
tweets.nap-18060610-329: I asked for a note on Prussia forces — Laforest letters are not it. I need the king of Prussia whole army stated plain.
tweets.nap-18060610-330: Yarmouth comes with full powers, and we agree but for Sicily — England recognizes you at Naples, not without the island. I conclude nothing till you hold the whole kingdom.
tweets.nap-18060619-331: Tell Alquier my two views of the Pope: temporal prince in my confederation, keep his states or lose every coast; spiritual chief — settle Italy or I plant the French Concordat there. True religion saves everywhere alike.
tweets.nap-18060629-332: Celerier poaches my Paris opera for Naples — ridiculous. I will send all the dancers you want, but stealing them is forbidden. Even Russia got my ballet girls, Gardel excepted. Spare Celerier — he is your architect.
tweets.nap-18060702-333: No news of Regnier — cut off, country risen. I chafe in Paris: give me Naples and no Englishman lands. With 36,000 men, let no division be crushed.
tweets.nap-18060710-334: Try the assassins of the blind men strikingly — I will publish it wide. All the world knows the Neapolitan queen atrocity; she cannot come home but over a sea of blood.
tweets.nap-18060726-335: Nine seminaries at once — report me priest numbers. Sound Gallican schooling against bad theology, and hurry the catechism.
tweets.nap-18060807-336: I send you Lucchesini letter — know the scamp I judged long ago as a deceiving wretch. Send Laforest a courier to enlighten Berlin: Haugwitz keeps ridiculous company, and this false base pantaloon proves true.
tweets.nap-18060810-337: Murat letters enclosed — send Laforest to Berlin confidentially. Cleves has orders: no hostilities toward Prussia. Tell them plainly: I refused England over Hanover precisely to spare Prussia, and want good terms at any price.
tweets.nap-18060810-338: Nuremberg prints libels — tell its Senate: arrest the booksellers and burn the sheets, or I punish the town before leaving Germany. Berthier has the same order for Augsburg: court-martial and shooting within a day.
tweets.nap-18060814-339: Thanks for my fête — affairs settle, and you shall have Paris voyage orders soon. I know you long to come. You will see Holland queen — we keep the princess till her confinement.
tweets.nap-18060907-340: I reached Mayence this morning — foot guards posted, guns and horse days behind.
tweets.nap-18061001-345: All goes as I hoped — God makes our affairs terrible for poor Prussia good king, and I pity him. I am well, even stouter; twenty leagues a day in saddle, carriage, everywhere. Bed at eight, up at midnight — I sometimes think you lie awake too.
tweets.nap-18061001-346: I deny it everywhere: no armistice — Murat and Ney are told. Prussia begged and was refused. Blücher duped Klein with 5,000 men and a six-week lie; their generals ape manners they lack.
tweets.nap-18061001-347: Your letter moves me — Madame de Hatzfeld suffering touched me. I convinced her: her husband is guilty, and war laws demand execution. Yet I spared him even a trial unpleasantness.
tweets.nap-18061014-348: Jena sends me an aide-de-camp with letters — Lucchesini waits at the outposts while Duroc learns his wants. The king leans to terms, but Berlin falls regardless.
tweets.nap-18061025-349: I crushed the Prussian monarchy; I shall crush the Russians if they come. No longer fear the Austrians. No troops needed from you -- But send cavalry if you can. I approve the ballet scenery; report on the return of Ulysses first representation to ensure nothing improper.
tweets.nap-18061101-350: Your letter -- you seem annoyed at my words on women. I dislike intriguing women; I love goodhearted, gentle ones. If they spoiled me, it is your fault. I was kind to Madame de Hatzfeld -- shown her husband's letter, she wept, recognizing his writing; her accent went to my heart.
tweets.nap-18061108-351: I am not a judge of your conduct, prince; it does not suit me to weigh your obligations. You say you were obliged to war against me -- you will not find it ill that I wish a prince at Fulde who is master to remain at peace with me.
tweets.nap-18061116-352: Received your letter -- my sentiments please you, but you are wrong to think I flatter. Sorry you do not amuse yourself at Mayence; if the voyage were shorter you could come -- no enemies this side of the Vistula. I wait your thoughts; would also gladly see Monsieur Napoleon.
tweets.nap-18061201-354: My troops entered Warsaw -- all Poland up in arms. Regiments raised by force; the richest most enthusiastic. Priests, nobles, peasants unanimous -- 60,000 men soon under arms. Great nobles fund their army. Amidst movements, festivities -- tomorrow a ball by the city nobility.
tweets.nap-18061201-355: Have a circular written: throughout the empire, all letters coming from England, or written in English by Englishmen, be seized. This is most important -- absolutely necessary to isolate England. Similar letter sent to Prince Eugene for my kingdom of Italy.
tweets.nap-18061201-356: Prussia, allied with Russia, has disappeared -- I destroyed her armies, hold her fortresses. My armies on the Vistula, Warsaw mine. Polish lands rising -- your moment to reconquer yours. Drive out rebel Hospodars; grant Serbians no concessions. Advance on Choczim.
tweets.nap-18061202-357: I write a line only, my Friend -- I am in a wretched barn. I have beaten the Russians, captured thirty guns, their baggage, and 6,000 men. Weather fearful; rains, mud up to the knee.
tweets.nap-18061214-358: My Friend -- starting for Warsaw, back in a fortnight when I hope to send for you. I should see you return to Paris, where you are desired, with pleasure. You know I depend on events -- all my affairs go well. Adieu, my friend. I have made peace with Saxony.
tweets.nap-18061231-359: Laughed at your last letter -- your Polish belles do not deserve the idea. Your letter reached me in a wretched barn: mud, wind, straw. Tomorrow Warsaw; year done, army into winter quarters. I shrug at Madame de L-- nonsense -- be angry, advise her not be foolish.
tweets.nap-18070102-363: Sir my Brother -- your wishes moved me. Our destinies placed vast countries between us -- you touch the Mediterranean, I the Baltic -- but our plans harmonize. Guard your coasts; drive off the English. Your kingdom rich, populous -- with God will be happy and powerful.
tweets.nap-18070107-364: Received your letter, thank you -- I prize your attachment. What are you doing in Paris? Heard no ball from you during Carnival. All great officers must spend money entertaining to keep Paris gay.
tweets.nap-18070114-365: Received your letter; Hesse Cassel is settled, the soldiery having moved on its own. The same day I wrote Holland king: trade runs as brisk as before my Berlin decree. Brother Louis must see to it.
tweets.nap-18070114-366: Turkey declared war against Russia -- a Tartar from Constantinople brings excellent news. A million forwarded to you from Turin. My health never better, consequence I have become more galant than formerly.
tweets.nap-18070116-367: My good friend -- your grief pains me. Why these tears? I shall soon see you; do not doubt my sentiments. Show greater strength of mind to be dearer to me. I feel humiliated that my wife can doubt my destinies.
tweets.nap-18070121-368: Your letter -- impossible to allow women such a journey: bad roads, dangerous, muddy. Return to Paris, be gay; perhaps I return soon. I laughed at taking a husband to be with him. I thought wife for husband, husband for country, family, glory -- forgive my error.
tweets.nap-18070203-373: My Friend -- great battle yesterday; I gained the victory but lost a great many men. Enemy loss still more considerable does not console me. I write these few lines myself, though very tired, to tell you I am well and that I love you.
tweets.nap-18070203-374: My dear friend -- you must have been anxious. I beat the enemy on a memorable day, but it cost many gallant lives. Bad weather forces cantonments. Do not be disconsolate -- all soon finished, seeing you will make me forget fatigues. Never felt better. Adieu, a thousand kisses.
tweets.nap-18070209-375: I send you a line, my Friend, lest you be uneasy. Enemy lost the battle, 40 guns, 12 standards, 12,000 prisoners; he suffered horridly. I lost 1,600 killed and between 3,000 and 4,000 wounded.
tweets.nap-18070220-376: I see conscription goes well. Sanguinary affair at Eylau on the eighth; my right at Ostralenka on the sixteenth -- Russians beaten both. No importance to Kosciusco -- not esteemed in his country, his conduct proves him a fool.
tweets.nap-18070310-381: I see Paris gossips more of Mlle Aubry than of all the army losses; Lugay wronged her by coldness. She who played Goddess of Reason now plays Glory, and fell breaking her arm before the Empress.
tweets.nap-18070401-382: I am delighted to hear nothing more of Madame de Stael -- when I trouble myself about her it is when I have facts before me. That woman is a regular crow; she thought she saw the tempest coming. Let her go to Her Lake Leman.
tweets.nap-18070404-383: My Son -- send Lauriston 25 watches for Turks, 25 to Marmont. You claim 20,000 men with grand army -- you dont believe it; you have 10,000, and what men! Make soldiers, not marshals, knights, counts. You govern Holland like a Capucin -- a king orders, asks nothing.
tweets.nap-18070414-384: Displeased with your preamble suppressing monasteries. In religion use language of religion, not philosophy -- the art of governing. Why speak of monks services to art and science? Your preamble philosophical, insults the evicted.
tweets.nap-18070502-386: My Friend -- I see with pleasure you are in good health and always fond of Malmaison. It is said the arch-chancellor has fallen in love -- is this a joke, or true? It greatly amuses me.
tweets.nap-18070601-387: Hope the week-finished campaign pleases my people. Russian army more crushed than ever the Austrians -- Beningsen showed little talent. Their soldiers good but weakened, discouraged. My army superb, unscathed. Conscription goes well.
tweets.nap-18070602-388: I have just seen the Emperor of Russia in the middle of the Niemen on a raft with a handsome flag. Tomorrow the Emperor presents the king of Prussia to me and comes to reside here -- I have neutralised Tilsit. I wish you to arrive as speedily as possible.
tweets.nap-18070615-389: My Friend -- few words, very tired, bivouacking days. My children celebrated Marengo anniversary. Friedland as glorious -- Russian army routed, 80 guns, 30,000 taken or killed, 25 generals; guard annihilated -- sister of Marengo, Austerlitz, Jena. My loss small.
tweets.nap-18070622-390: While St. Denis unready, place the little Napoleon's body in Notre Dame chapel. Proclamation: Frenchmen, worthy of yourselves and me -- return with laurels after glorious, durable peace. Time for country to live in repose from England. My recompenses prove my gratitude and love.
tweets.nap-18070701-391: My Friend -- queen of Prussia dined with me. I defended against further concessions to her husband; galant but adhered to policy. She is very amiable. When you read this, peace concluded with Russia and Prussia, Jerome king of Westphalia.
tweets.nap-18070701-392: The queen of Prussia is really charming; she is full of coquetterie towards me. But do not be jealous -- I am an oilcloth off which all that runs. It would cost me too dear to play the galant.
tweets.nap-18070701-393: Guilleminot to Michelson HQ, then Grand Vizir -- inform peace concluded, treaty articles for Porte. Then Constantinople with cipher to Sebastiani -- tell my ambassador my system on Porte shaky, changing; not decided; greatest friendship with Russia.
tweets.nap-18070706-395: I see with pain you are an egotist -- the success of my arms has no attraction for you. The handsome queen of Prussia comes to dine with me today. I am in good health and greatly wish to see you when destiny permits -- probability not long.
tweets.nap-18070714-396: Sir my Brother -- to express viva voce the sentiments you inspire, I send my aide-de-camp Savary, appointed ambassador to your court. Receive him with your peculiar kindness.
tweets.nap-18070722-397: I Write Alquier to insist on French cardinals number. Russians ill-treat poor and rich -- plunder, burn, massacre: their amusements. Austerlitz a European victory -- destroyed prestige of these barbarians. No European government will call such fatal aid again.
tweets.nap-18070922-401: Lima saw Murat without presentation -- duty as my brother-in-law, grand admiral, reigning prince. My displeasure. Metternich presented properly. With Segur, report on ambassador reception. All settled before Friday for Russian ambassador.
tweets.nap-18070925-402: I send for Izquierdo on Spain debt, Portugal, Etruria. Portugal: I see no difficulty giving Spain suzerainty, portion for Etruria queen and prince of peace. Etruria: difficult Spanish branch in Italy now all Italy mine.
tweets.nap-18071007-403: Courier to Junot: enter Spain in 24 hours, march Portugal. Ambassador left Lisbon -- no moment to lose. To Charles IV: Holland, confederation, you, Alexander, I unite to drive English, avenge Denmark -- Portugal last resistance.
tweets.nap-18071014-404: I send for province descriptions, roads, ground. Sketches by engineers -- village distances, nature, resources. I do not leave my army -- a general never leaves it; great only with it, small at court. Portugal war on England not enough -- I march on.
tweets.nap-18071101-405: Marescalchi sends me Spain treaty -- Tuscany mine, I unite to Italy. Leghorn troops suffice, I prepare secretly. Lucca coins: Napoleon protege l Italia not suitable; replacing Dieu protege la France indecent.
tweets.nap-18071201-406: I saw Lucien at Mantua -- he promised daughter to Paris by winter. Lucien conflicted, lacked decision. I urged him to serve me and country. Daughter must start with declaration at my disposal. No moment lost. Events march. I await answer on Charlotte.
tweets.nap-18080107-407: My Brother -- Brunswick petition. No reply -- he omitted subject in letter, you recognise only subjects. Brunswick prince presence damaging, not permitted. In 2-3 years retirement ok. Meanwhile no reply.
tweets.nap-18080301-413: I published the four-million contribution before mastering the country. Since entering Portugal you did nothing I desired. The Portuguese troops should have marched for France long since, reaching Bayonne for me to organise. You left the forts months in Portuguese hands.
tweets.nap-18080302-414: My Son -- Cardinal Ruffo (Calabrias) to Paris, Cardinal Ruffo Scylla (Naples archbishop) to Bologna, two dangerous cardinals removed. Miollis: no arrangement with Rome; orders contempt, seize temporal government. Battalions through Vatican. Allow Lent before settling Rome.
tweets.nap-18080310-415: Approve Miollis -- treat Roman soldiers well, dismiss bad officers. Send Neapolitan and my cardinals from Rome: Litta to Milan, Genoese to Genoa, Italians to Italy, Piedmontese to Piedmont, Neapolitans to Naples. Caraffa responsible for stone from window.
tweets.nap-18080316-416: Ordered Neapolitan cardinals at Rome sent to you for allegiance. You sent them to Alessandria -- I cannot understand. What fear from 2-3 old priests? Oath excellent effect. Pope calls you Prince Joseph, makes your cardinals refuse oath. If you fear 2-3 old men, throne insecure.
tweets.nap-18080401-417: Received your letter with queen, Charlotte, Zenaide. At Bayonne. Infant Don Carlos ill. Expect Ferdinand VII on frontier, King Charles and queen. To Ferdinand: father papers show my interest in your family.
tweets.nap-18080401-418: I see ambassador language in Paris -- hardly believe Tolstoy used attributed words, a quolibet. My Reply: couriers brought Moldavia rupture, Finland conquest, fresh troops. Courts on best terms. My quarrels Rome/Spain nothing to do with Russia. Good terms with all.
tweets.nap-18080501-419: Spanish ambassador complains papers say Charles forced abdication. I tell him: I saw king and queen receive son badly; under poinard hours, would perish if refused. Prince Asturias stupid, bad-hearted, enemy of France. I arrested couriers -- letters hate French.
tweets.nap-18080501-420: I say confidentially: Charles gets Compiegne for life, Chambord, forest, 30M real pension. He cedes Spanish throne. Charles excellent. Starts tomorrow, week Fontainebleau. Asturias no interest -- so stupid no word drawn. Madrid and Burgos lesson decides.
tweets.nap-18080501-421: I Write Laforest: regret ambassador weakness; enlighten Duke of Berg, not pander; counterpoise not lead to follies. Junta and Castille sharper than my lieutenant-general; hesitation from unknown renunciations; no voice for Murat; nation in hatred, desires him less.
tweets.nap-18080503-422: Congratulate on son -- name Charles Napoleon. Christened Charles Louis Napoleon. Sent Murat two I the king documents handing government to French Emperor. Proclamation: against France = thirst for blood, enemies, English agents.
tweets.nap-18080601-423: King of Naples arrived, acknowledged Spain king, leaving for Madrid. Oath from grandees, Castille, India, Inquisition. Dupont 15k at Seville, Saragossa revolted. King arrival ends disturbances. English king death -- great joy to me.
tweets.nap-18080707-424: I Send Alexander Spanish Junta constitution. Disorder inconceivable. New situation: Spain more independent of me. I am satisfied with rank, fortune, education. Monks and Inquisition agitate. If only France interest, I extend frontiers at Spain expense -- tie broken.
tweets.nap-18080802-425: I Send Villoutreys on Dupont. Vedel, Gobert not in affair -- cowards capitulated for baggage. Frenchmen such cowardice! Note: war men nothing, a man all. Examples only in enemy history; unfortunate none in ours.
tweets.nap-18080810-426: I Write Caulaincourt: Alexander twentieth summer -- aids if Austria war, anxious on Spain. Step full of feeling. To Berthier: intercepted Spanish letters. Send to Bernadotte -- suppose he broke correspondence.
tweets.nap-18080910-427: Marescot signed infamous capitulation -- I deprived employment. Madame Marescot cannot remain lady in waiting. Crime: not responsible for Baylen but sanctioned capitulation. Paid dearly for generosity.
tweets.nap-18080910-428: Caulaincourt: Alexander leaves Erfurth twelfth. I send Lannes to Vistula to meet you. To Soult: papers on Stein letter. I demanded dismissal from Ministry or Prussia king not return. I sequestered Westphalia property. Austria far from war. I am sure of Russia.
tweets.nap-18080914-429: Madam my Sister -- delighted your Berlin return, my dearest wish. King and you resume former sentiments. To Spain king at Miranda: no reply to bad temper -- principle. Too much intelligence not to understand this only response.
tweets.nap-18081001-430: My Friend -- well. Shooting Jena field -- breakfasted where bivouacked. Weimar ball: Alexander danced, not I; forty years forty years. Health good despite ailing. Erfurth convention: Finland, Moldavia, Wallachia Russian = peace with England condition.
tweets.nap-18081014-431: Concluded all with Alexander. Start tomorrow Paris, Bayonne within month. Send exact army report. War closable by single manoeuvre, I must be there. Reduced Prussia contribution 20M; told Austria never supposed hostilities resume.
tweets.nap-18081101-432: I just arrived. Troops scattered -- write me twice daily for corps positions. I rode Landes at gallop, tired. Fourth: Tolosa, Vittoria next night, orders to Moncey, Ney, Berthier. Spanish defeats: Castanos Logrono, Blake Durango, Burgos. Eleventh I entered Burgos.
tweets.nap-18081126-433: Tudela matches Espinosa. Andalusia under Castanos, Aragon under Palafox, Valentia and new Castile, all broken and scattered; guns, baggage and prisoners taken. Then Somo-Sierra: my Polish lancers carried the battery.
tweets.nap-18070804-398: I do not know what rash act you suppose the Pope capable of. You should have sent troops toward Bologna -- if he commits an imprudence, a fine opportunity to deprive him of the Roman states. I wrote the king of Wurtemberg for Princess Catherine for my Brother Jerome.
tweets.nap-18070810-399: I am proprietor in Warsaw of all debts due to the king of Prussia by private individuals -- money advanced on land security, 60M francs. War requisitions: Germany 24.2M, Italy 1.2M, Spain 2.88M, Portugal 0.64M, Austria 2M arrears. Total 30.92M.
tweets.nap-18080217-412: Whence come journal details on Caulaincourt? The Publiciste should not praise Lambert. I order articles describing him as a traitor who fought against his country. Savary coldly received in Russia -- nobility houses closed.
tweets.nap-18090301-439: I hasten to inform you I have deemed fit to create your Son Prince Napoleon Louis Grand Duke of Berg. You were vexed at this creation without consulting you. Saragossa fell after heroic resistance. A stain on Lannes: he violated capitulation, executed two gallant defenders.
tweets.nap-18090321-440: I received your letter. War appears imminent. Best thing: assemble troops to defend your country and serve the common cause. First time you ask my advice.
tweets.nap-18090501-441: My Friend -- I received your letter. The bullet which touched me did not wound me -- barely shaved the Achilles tendon. My health very good; you are wrong to feel uneasy. My affairs go well.
tweets.nap-18090519-442: You greatly alarmed Paris about Prussia. Even if she attacked us, Prussia is of no consequence, easily subdued. You have not shown sufficient prudence -- bad effect when a power thinks I am not in position to fight. In ninth bulletin: throwing bridge across Danube.
tweets.nap-18090601-443: I reply to your letter on Carnot. If he merely helped relieve Manberige he would have my gratitude. As War minister he has right to a pension. I make no difficulty employing him as he wishes. Let me know his embarrassments. Carnot, entirely ruined, applied for army employment.
tweets.nap-18090701-444: I send a page with good news: victory at Enzersdorf and Wagram. Enemy army flying in disorder. Everything goes according to my wishes. Eugene well. Aldobrandini slightly wounded; Bessieres thigh grazed. Lasalle killed.
tweets.nap-18090701-445: I see the bull of excommunication is so ridiculous it does not deserve attention. What deserves attention: provide for vacant sees. Must know what Pope intends -- if he does not confirm bishops per Concordat he will create a schism.
tweets.nap-18090710-446: You know my intentions on a Tyrol expedition. Be at Innsbruck by summer. No ridiculous proclamations; be severe; disarm the country; take many hostages and make examples. Act with celerity.
tweets.nap-18090722-447: Prince Liechtenstein handed me your Majesty's letter, in which you inform me that you have appointed negotiators to treat for peace.
tweets.nap-18090801-448: What a lost hour! Thirty thousand English, far from the sea, facing a hundred thousand of the world's best troops! Had Soult joined, one blow could have ended it. I blame hesitation, and I will have energy.
tweets.nap-18090801-449: It is repugnant to my feelings to suppose Flushing surrendered -- that appears impossible. Such conduct would be cowardice approaching treason. Flushing can defend itself as long as it has a morsel of bread. Enemy cannot have destroyed inundation means.
tweets.nap-18090901-450: You have no confidence in Abbe de Pradt. I do not know if I told you to distrust that man as greatest enemy we can have. Profound hypocrite, neither morality nor talent of his condition, addicted to intrigue leading to scaffold. Treat him as usual, let this remain secret.
tweets.nap-18090904-451: I saw in Moniteur details you inserted on Spain; they are not sufficient. This does not compensate for immense English relations. Publish letters of different generals, effacing what is for government only. Letters from Soult, Moncey, Sebastiani should be published.
tweets.nap-18091007-452: I write to king of Spain: English reports claim they took guns, state number; all army letters certify this; Senarmont says six guns taken. Find how many lost at Talavera -- slightest omission criminal; not for publication, to know truth.
tweets.nap-18091010-453: Reports this morning show enemy retreating as fast as he can. Battlefield covered with dead. I am about to get on horseback to examine situation, attack if he occupies positions, pursue if falling back. To king of Saxony: I wrote from battlefield.
tweets.nap-18091021-454: I arrived here yesterday in good health. Stop a day at Stuttgart. You shall receive 24 hours notice of my arrival at Fontainebleau. Great pleasure to see you again, await with impatience. I embrace you.
tweets.nap-18091028-455: I beg you write an historical sketch proving: popes always enemies of power predominating in Italy. When Germans triumphed they called the French; when French masters they leagued with Germans to drive them out.
tweets.nap-18091121-456: Tell Spain's king: had Ney stayed at Salamanca, my army had suffered no such affront. Marchand cannot command in chief. When I send marshals I feel the need; no method rules this Spanish campaign. Del Parque's Spaniards beat us and hold Salamanca, answer it.
tweets.nap-18091122-457: I see with pleasure you arrived at Milan. You wrote a work on your Italian campaign -- send it to me. My financial affairs here in great disorder. English expedition cost 2M. New levies and immense armaments for Spain continue to ruin me.
tweets.nap-18091201-458: My brother, Roumanzoff's second note grieves me. Why reopen what my Vienna letter settled? I declared before Europe my will on Warsaw, Moldavia, Wallachia. What more is asked? I cannot slay chimeras and fight clouds. Judge whose language fits alliance: yours or mine.
tweets.nap-18100106-459: I write to Rome for the fisherman ring, the seals of the pontiff, the ornaments of the tiara, everything used by the Pope in ceremonies. At seizure of Pope papers a packet of golden pieces found in Doria portfolio, returned without remark that the fisherman ring was among them.
tweets.nap-18100127-460: Write Laforest at Madrid: present notes on impossibility of meeting Spain enormous expenses; I already sent 300M francs there; such sums exhaust France. Add war with Austria cost much. Much money in provinces.
tweets.nap-18100206-461: Send a courier to Caulaincourt tonight. The council splits between a Russian and an Austrian match, and France over religion. As for the Princess Anne talk, girls ripen late; I note it and move on.
tweets.nap-18100212-462: I beg you send for the Dutch minister. Tell him Police minister had interviews with king of Holland, who desires to conciliate his country independence with my views, proposes: first cede left bank of Rhine to France; second stop all communication with England.
tweets.nap-18100223-463: I hasten to inform you the marriage contract between myself and Archduchess Marie Louise, daughter of the Emperor of Austria, was ratified at Vienna. Similar letters to all imperial family.
tweets.nap-18100301-464: I attach great importance to Congreve rockets. As soon as fabrication success established, send to Spain against Cadiz, Ciudad-Rodrigo, Badajoz -- forward to seventh and Third Army Corps in Catalonia and Aragon.
tweets.nap-18100302-465: My theatres play Mort dAbel in spring; Persie et Andromide Easter Monday; Bayaderes a fortnight after; Sophoch and Armede in summer; Danaides in autumn; Sabines at spring end. I want the calendar full.
tweets.nap-18100403-466: I do not consider it right you should issue a proclamation.
tweets.nap-18100425-467: I wrote to send away the Persian ambassador, but without treating him badly. Tell him I do not wish to see him, displeased Persia sold political interests to the English.
tweets.nap-18100501-468: You must deny report of Moreau recall, state that general, whose intrigues with Bourbons are well known, is forever excluded from France.
tweets.nap-18100501-469: I reckon you will have ten vessels in roads by summer, yet I have heard of no movement in Holland. Think how important this is for the common cause, keep your engagements. POSITION of two brothers: Napoleon hardly seated Louis on Holland throne when quarrels began.
tweets.nap-18100501-470: I write to king of Spain: sorry to see extensive arming of Spaniards, only prolongs resistance, causes French blood to flow; when so often deceived difficult to understand such obstinacy.
tweets.nap-18100516-471: Caulaincourt informed me of all amiable things your Majesty said on my marriage. Accept my thanks. My feelings towards you as unchangeable as political principles governing my empire relations. Never will your Majesty have to complain of France.
tweets.nap-18100518-472: Present lucid note to Prussian ambassador on prince of Hatzfeld affair: dwell on scandal of trial, how it displeases me, I recognise the hand of that cabal drawing down misfortunes.
tweets.nap-18100529-473: Inform king of Spain: I cannot send regiment Joseph-Napoleon, animated with such bad spirit officers demanded its withdrawal from Spain frontiers; he can judge how impolitic and inconsiderate his Spanish levies are.
tweets.nap-18070826-400: English at Copenhagen, bombarding. Russia should march on Sweden for Denmark. Alexander need only say -- I do all necessary. Army at Hamburg. If English continue: close all European ports, expel ambassadors, arrest individuals. Joint declaration to Austria if Emperor agrees.
tweets.nap-18080201-408: Sir my Brother -- Savary arrived, we spoke hours of your Majesty. English parliament continues war. Caulaincourt has my opinion. Only large measures bring peace. Augment your army -- I help fully. No jealousy vs Russia; desire her glory, prosperity, extension.
tweets.nap-18080201-409: Courier to Constantinople on Algiers. Turkish ambassador: condescendence for Porte delays expedition; but if slaves not freed by return courier, I seize Algiers.
tweets.nap-18080211-410: My Son -- my troops entered Rome on the second, consul and Queen Caroline agents arrested. Write Miollis: take police, treat Papal troops well, drive out Neapolitan rebels, even cardinals.
tweets.nap-18080214-411: My Son -- recalled Alquier. Miollis pay difficulties at Rome. Must ensure troops want nothing; if Rome cannot furnish, Miollis takes government and ecclesiastical provinces except Ancona, Camerino, Urbino, Macerata under Lemarrois. Secret: possible I go to Rome soon.
tweets.nap-18090101-434: Pope sends tapers. Rome agent: I refuse. Spain refuses. Naples, Holland refuse -- papal court offered none last year. Charge d'affaires: Candlemas I receive tapers blessed by my cure -- not purple or power gives value. Popes and cures in hell; my cure taper as holy.
tweets.nap-18090101-435: My Son -- Battaglia: Augusta another princess. I hope next a boy. Ninth: two letters to Spain king -- solemn Madrid entry, well received; councils, ministers administer. Second: English flight, money convoy captured. English full retreat.
tweets.nap-18090201-436: Madam my Sister -- your interest in Spanish arms agreeable, thank you. Sorry king health poor, but spring and Geroux waters salutary.
tweets.nap-18090225-437: Sir my Brother -- thank you for interest in my return, congratulations on victories. Would have liked your Majesty in good health.
tweets.nap-18090301-438: My Son -- Cesarotti history of popes; if shows harm to religion, publish. Next day to German vassals: Vienna news requires contingents without delay.
tweets.nap-18100610-474: Report the missing conscripts. I might post them dangerously: ship them to Corsica, form six or seven thousand for Sardinia under a good general and colonels. Idleness breeds desertion; give them an island to take.
tweets.nap-18100610-475: I wrote to you yesterday for the letter which M. Fagan brought back from Lord Wellesley. I write to you again today to let you know that you must hand to me, with that letter, all the documents, without exception, concerning Ouvrard, Labouchere, and Fagan.
tweets.nap-18100610-476: Instruct Oudinot: once his Utrecht force can march on Amsterdam, let him write my charge that French troops were insulted and Haarlem shut its gates. Demand amends. My eagles enter every friendly land.
tweets.nap-18100614-477: I have read your report on the subject of the dispute between my Consul and the Dey of Algiers. My agent seems to me very culpable; he should not compromise my interests for such trifles. Make known to him my displeasure. Let M. Thainville settle this affair.
tweets.nap-18100710-480: I plant press pieces on Russian wins in Turkey and the coming peace: Moldavia and Wallachia ceded, and vessels falsely claimed from Teneriffe seized, English goods in truth.
tweets.nap-18100720-481: MADAME -- I hasten to inform you that the king of Holland is at Teplitz in Bohemia. As you must have experienced some uneasiness on his disappearance, I do not lose a moment in sending you this news to tranquillise you.
tweets.nap-18100721-482: Sir, my Brother and Father-in-Law -- Allow me to send your Imperial majesty a porcelain cup from my manufactory of Sevres upon which the portrait of Louise is painted. I hope that this present will be agreeable to your Majesty, and that you will find it well done.
tweets.nap-18100726-483: Have a courier ready to convey my letter to the Emperor of Austria. Write to M. Otto to demand the arrest of Pozzo di Borgo as having been condemned to death by default for having betrayed France in favour of England.
tweets.nap-18100726-484: Summon this director to Paris to answer for himself, and report him fully to me. I will know why the Hercule's business miscarried. My service suffers no sleepy agents.
tweets.nap-18100819-486: I have received no details respecting my army of Catalonia. I am ignorant of the manner in which Macdonald has made his movement, what troops he has taken with him, and what cantonments he has left behind him. My Army of Catalonia is the only one of which I have no news.
tweets.nap-18100822-487: I have received your letter of the, in which you tell me that 200 Englishmen have been removed from the Irish regiment.
tweets.nap-18100918-489: I hear everywhere the rumour of Prince Ferdinand's pretended match with an Austrian princess, and I credit it.
tweets.nap-18100918-490: I have read with surprise a letter from the major of the Irish regiment. I never ordered that the Irishmen who fought for me at Flushing, and who were wounded in my service, should be sent back among the prisoners. I can therefore understand nothing of this gossip.
tweets.nap-18100920-491: Write to Prussia, and speak to M. de Krusemark here, saying that I should like to see the Prussian government lay a duty on the export of cereals. England is in want of corn, and it will be useful and agreeable to Prussia to levy this contribution from her.
tweets.nap-18100921-492: The idea of sending Spaniards to Corfu is bad. Give orders for the Spaniards to be sent to Toulon. At Corfu they would consume provisions, and would betray us on the first opportunity. They must be sent into the interior.
tweets.nap-18101001-493: If there are any monks among the Spanish prisoners, you must make them throw off their frocks on crossing the frontier, and have them dressed with coats and mixed up with the other prisoners.
tweets.nap-18101013-494: I send you a draft of instructions for M. De Nerciat. I wish this agent for the present to visit only Syria and Egypt; he must pay attention to St.
tweets.nap-18101014-495: I send you a letter from General Rapp.
tweets.nap-18101017-496: I forward a letter, which has just fallen into my hands. Write to M. Otto (ambassador at Vienna) to forewarn him on the subject of the false rumours it contains. Speak in the Moniteur of the presents which I made M.
tweets.nap-18101101-497: Have all the merchandise of English manufacture in Holland, in the warehouses, shops, etc., burned at once. My finances are in the most prosperous condition. I can meet all the expenses of this immense empire without demanding any new sacrifices on the part of my people.
tweets.nap-18101112-499: Send my Berne minister the Valais reunion decree, sealed till Caesar Berthier plants my troops in Sion and holds the land. Let him call it proof of Swiss freedom, settling Italy and Switzerland for good. I take what the blockade demands.
tweets.nap-18101118-500: Send me the draft of a reply to Prince Kourakine, very polite, very moderate, but which nevertheless shall contain those truths which it is fit that Russia should know.
tweets.nap-18101201-501: I send you a report on the losses of Westphalia. You argue as if Hanover belonged to Westphalia. Hanover does not belong to the King Jerome, for that prince not having executed the treaty which he concluded with me, I look upon it as null and void.
tweets.nap-18110101-503: They have just discovered a party of the Pope here. An Abbe Gregori and an Abbe Fontana, whom I brought here from Rome, were the intermediaries of a correspondence between the Pope and the Vicars-General of Paris.
tweets.nap-18110129-504: I send you back your report on Papal affairs; I find it incorrect. For instance, the union of the Papal states to the empire did not take place until the Pope was at Savona. You must not speak of the marriage and the legitimacy of the child; that is too absurd.
tweets.nap-18110201-505: Tell the Transport Office: among prisoners sits Kolli, self-styled Irishman, bearing England's letter and a minister's commission to Ferdinand. I will trade him for equal rank.
tweets.nap-18110225-506: I have read with attention the letters from Stockholm. There is so much effervescence and turmoil in the head of the prince of Sweden, that I attach no importance to the communication he has addressed to Baron Alquier.
tweets.nap-18110301-507: I have received your report on the Irish regiment. Send me a more detailed report, informing me if the officers of that corps are Irish, and if there are means of creating an Irish regiment principally recruited among Germans.
tweets.nap-18110310-508: I send a courier to st. Petersburg with a letter from General Lauriston to count romanzoff, announcing his approaching departure, his desire to be agreeable, and the hope that his mission will meet with the approbation of the Czar.
tweets.nap-18110402-509: I forward you a report from Marshal Marmont with regard to the request of Prince Schwartzenberg relative to affairs in Illyria. You should see the marshal in order to draw up a reply, and try if it would not be better to settle the mortmain affairs.
tweets.nap-18110613-511: I beg that you will write a letter to the transport office, demanding the return to France of all the prisoners who are in England, captured at Baylen with Dupont's army. Put forward some reasons to show how just this would be.
tweets.nap-18110621-512: I beg that you will hint gently to the Swedish ambassador that I regret to see the Princess royal arrive in France without having obtained permission; that this is not usual, and that I am sorry she should have left her husband at so critical a moment.
tweets.nap-18110704-513: Send for O'Connor and the Paris Irish; raise an Irish party. I hold twenty-five sail in the Scheldt, nine at Texel. I lean to landing thirty thousand foot and four thousand horse. I will sign whatever Ireland asks.
tweets.nap-18110801-514: I shall make no difficulty about granting Prussia licences for the exportation of Silesian cloths. Demand that Prussia shall no longer receive any colonial produce coming from Russia.
tweets.nap-18110801-515: I send you a letter from a soldier in garrison at Stettin. He says that there are a great many men on the sick list. I thought that the air of Stettin was good. Take care to have my Troops quartered in places where no sickness is to be feared.
tweets.nap-18110801-516: Let me know what day my troops can embark at Cherbourg. When will all the vessels be there? I have a great many relations with Ireland. I already hold the thread which sets a good many things in motion. My agents begin to come and go.
tweets.nap-18110823-518: Rate Soult through Berthier: sending Albuera trophies by an Austrian hireling insults me. The fellow fought against us. I expect my marshals to know their messengers.
tweets.nap-18110824-519: It is necessary for you to write again to my minister at Carlsruhe. The Princess Stephanie is wrong to show a preference for Manheim; her duty is to be with her husband.
tweets.nap-18110918-521: I have read with interest the letter of General O'Connor, which I return. It appears very important to me to establish relations with Ireland. Ask for particulars with regard to the state of public opinion at present.
tweets.nap-18111026-522: From this place I intend going to the Grand Duchy of Berg, and afterwards to Fontainebleau. I am extremely satisfied with the Dutch.
tweets.nap-18111101-523: I beg that you will see the queen of Spain and Tell her that I wish the princess of Sweden to leave Paris and return to Stockholm.
tweets.nap-18111101-524: I am informed that you have made a present of some horses to the Prince royal of Sweden. I desire that you countermand the despatch of these horses. Sweden is behaving very badly, and at any moment we may go to war. These gifts are therefore not proper at the present moment.
tweets.nap-18111206-525: Nesselrode's coming decides me: I raise the conscription. Bid the Confederation princes remount horse and ready contingents, pleading Russia's mass levy, her crowded frontier, her bent for war. To my foreign minister: in war Bignon joins my staff to head secret police.
tweets.nap-18120106-527: In the Reveries of Marshal Saxe, amid a great many things extremely mediocre, there are some ideas on the way of raising contributions in the enemy's country without fatiguing the army, which appear to me to be good.
tweets.nap-18120108-528: I await with impatience your report upon the colonial merchandise which you have found in Pomerania. You have, no doubt, sent a detachment of custom-house officers there.
tweets.nap-18120114-529: You have given the command of the department of the Apennines to Adjutant Commander Bourmont, that is to say to an old Chouan leader. This measure is ridiculous. That officer should not be employed, or employed only in such a way as to be under supervision.
tweets.nap-18120202-530: The reports from Toulon, as well as accounts from England, show that my squadron manoeuvred badly, and that it ought to have captured two English frigates which were allowed to escape.
tweets.nap-18120216-531: I m. Is not fit for the foreign office. He is said to be imbued with English customs and tastes, and that he likes and prefers the individuals of that nation to other people. This, in a French agent, is very inconvenient. M.
tweets.nap-18120227-532: I send you the papers of the Committee of inquiry on the capitulation of Dupont at Baylen, I beg that you will read them with care and draw up a report. You must join to the report a demand on the part of Comte Regnaud for the convocation of the High court.
tweets.nap-18120301-533: It is time to finish with this scandal of the Sisters of Charity who have revolted against the Superioresses. It is my intention to suppress the convents which, within twenty-four hours after being warned, have not submitted.
tweets.nap-18120312-535: Tell Marmont: holding five English divisions beyond the Tagus clears him; if Badajos falls to two, blame the south army alone. I judge commanders by results.
tweets.nap-18120328-536: I send you a report on the Russian army furnished by the Prussians. Ask Prince Schwartzenberg to communicate to you the ideas of Vienna upon it. It seems to me that this report gives three divisions too many.
tweets.nap-18120616-538: I tell you Ney corps strays from its traced route, ravaging everywhere.
tweets.nap-18120702-540: Today our van seized eight guns and seven hundred men. Russia lies at Vitebsk. I tell you privately, write nothing of it. We stand on the edge of great events.
tweets.nap-18120801-541: I have this instant returned to my quarters; the heat is excessive, and there is a great deal of dust, which fatigues us a little. We had the whole Russian army here; it received orders to deliver battle, and did not dare. We carried Smolensko by assault.
tweets.nap-18120826-543: The enemy, after having constructed fortifications, raised batteries and redoubts, and announced their intention of making a stand here, as usual, failed in resolution. We entered this town, which is considerable enough, as it has eight or ten steeples.
tweets.nap-18120902-545: I have received the report of Marshal Marmont on the battle of Salamanca. It is impossible to read anything more paltry; there is more noise and more clatter in it than in a clock, and not a word to explain the real state of affairs.
tweets.nap-18120910-546: It is supposed that Wittgenstein has left the Drissa in order to take up a position between Moscow and St. Petersburg. Should this turn out to be true, write to Marshal St. Cyr to pursue him, and to arrive at the same time as the enemy, in order to cover my flank.
tweets.nap-18121010-548: I on the or Marshal Mortier must set fire to the eau-de-vie stores, the barracks, and to the public establishments, with the exception of the foundling hospital. He must set fire to the palace of the Kremlin.
tweets.nap-18121016-549: I have received your letter of the, and thank you for the feelings you express. It is I who am indebted to you for the excellent care which you take of the little king; I am exceedingly grateful for it.
tweets.nap-18121102-550: I have received your letter of the, in which you say nothing about France, and give me no news of Spain. And yet for the last fortnight I have received no news, no estafette, and I am in the dark as concerns everything.
tweets.nap-18121214-554: I remain a moment at Dresden in order to write to your Majesty. In spite of great fatigue my health never was better. I started on the, after the battle of Beresina, from Lithuania, leaving the Grand army under the orders of the king of Naples.
tweets.nap-18121218-555: We are terribly fatigued and half starved. Send bread, meat, and brandy to meet us. I have 100,000 stragglers who are trying to live, and who are no longer under the colours. This causes us to run horrible dangers. My Old guard alone maintains its ranks, but hunger is gaining it.
tweets.nap-18121218-556: Most Holy Father, I send my household officer with joy at your mending health; summer alarms proved hollow. Your new residence lets us meet; despite all, my friendship stands.
tweets.nap-18130101-557: Send Duroc for the inventor; prove his musket with my Guard gunners, trial it, report to me. I love a new arm.
tweets.nap-18130101-558: According to custom, I consider it right, on important occasions, to make known our situation to your Majesty. Your Majesty has learned from the published reports the victories which I have gained over the Russian armies. I did not once meet them without beating them.
tweets.nap-18130101-559: I have received your letter of the. I have already told you that I see the command of the army in your hands with pleasure. I find the conduct of the king of Naples very extravagant, and such that it would require very little for me to have him arrested by way of an example.
tweets.nap-18130107-560: Boulogne camp dissolves; quarter the troops in town. To Berthier: yours with its strange news received. York's treason decides me. I speak to the nation and ordain a mighty levy. I form an army of observation.
tweets.nap-18130126-561: All your efforts should tend towards preserving Warsaw.
tweets.nap-18130131-562: I Reiterate orders for the king of Spain to remove his head-quarters to valladolid, to occupy Madrid only with the extremity of his left, and to send considerable forces to subdue the north of Spain.
tweets.nap-18130201-563: The viceroy writes to me that General Bülow has only 300 cavalry, and that therefore Prussia, instead of joining with us to defend her territory, and to repair the treason of General York, does nothing.
tweets.nap-18130202-564: I Order Admiral baste to go to Swedish Pomerania, where he will be, under the orders of General Morand, charged with the command of the flotilla, and to adopt measures for the defence of the isle of rugen and the coasts. He must visit the mouths of the oder.
tweets.nap-18130210-565: Her hopes know no bounds. She barters my finest provinces for treason and prices peace at my Empire's dismemberment. I read the offer plain and I refuse it.
tweets.nap-18130218-566: England fattens Portugal to thrust into Spain or land on my coast while I face north. Warn Spain's king: he squandered idle months when England could do nothing, never taming Navarre, Biscay, Aragon. Ever begging coin, he lets Mina waste my provinces.
tweets.nap-18130301-567: I beg that you will let me know if my palaces of Strasburg and of Mayence are in a good condition. They may be useful either for me or for the families of some of the princes of the confederation.
tweets.nap-18130302-568: I have received your letter from Leipsic. As soon as you receive news of General Morand, let me know, even the rumours which may reach you. By our latest news it appears still undecided whether Prussia will take the field against us.
tweets.nap-18130312-569: Magdeburg must live by requisition, as war has always allowed; Italy in my last campaign, Strasburg and Mayence lived so. Do there what I did there. You dream millions while I count the cost of three hundred thousand men.
tweets.nap-18130313-570: I return you the letter of the Bishop of Nantes. You must inform him that the form of the oath cannot be changed; that it could only be changed if it contained anything contrary to the mysteries of religion. All the pretensions of the cardinals are ridiculous.
tweets.nap-18130313-571: I approve of the measures taken for the defence of the Pyrenees, and for calling out the National guard.
tweets.nap-18130401-572: I grieve for Dresden bridge, Davoust's blast, yet money mends what powder breaks; some hundred thousand francs. To Jerome I wrote the same lesson: war devours coin, count it closely.
tweets.nap-18130401-573: I have reason to be satisfied with the intentions of Austria. I do not suspect her preparations; however, it is not my intention to be dependent upon her. The vulnerable part as regards Austria is my kingdom of Italy whither I intend to send the viceroy as soon as possible.
tweets.nap-18130402-574: Tell Spain's king I gave him my armies' chief command; his endless disobeyed complaints come from mixing Spain's king with my generalissimo. My armies answer no Spanish minister. From France expect nothing now.
tweets.nap-18130413-575: These are the plans for my departure; I shall start with you in a light carriage; the Grand marshal and the Comte de Lobau in another carriage; Fain and Yvan in a third. The three carriages must be all equally light.
tweets.nap-18130417-576: I reached Mayence in forty hours, in good health and without accident. The carriage of the Grand marshal has not yet rejoined me. I shall remain here for several days to look after a great many things which are wanting. To Berthier: send a courier to the king of Bavaria.
tweets.nap-18130418-577: I send you a letter from Comte de Mercy. I am extremely dissatisfied with the manner in which I am seconded by my Minister of Foreign affairs (M. Maret, due de Bassano).
tweets.nap-18130420-578: I have received your letter of the. The conjectures made with regard to the fidelity of the king of Saxony are absurd; neither the opinions nor the probity of that prince are known. You should deny these rumours with all your force.
tweets.nap-18130501-579: Sir, my Brother, and very dear Father-in-Law, What your Majesty said in your letter on the subject of the interest you bear me greatly affected me. I deserve this in consequence of my loyal feeling towards you.
tweets.nap-18130503-580: I am sorry that you did not advise the Empress to pardon the man condemned to death. You acted too much like a magistrate in that affair. Take the first opportunity of making the Empress accord one or two pardons on her own initiative.
tweets.nap-18130507-581: Send the inclosed letter to M. de Serra at Prague. The Emperor has arrived at Dresden. Tomorrow the army will pass the river in pursuit of the enemy. Inclosed you will find a letter on the subject of the conduct of General Thielman. You must tell M.
tweets.nap-18130510-582: Dresden is mine, both banks and Elbe forts; Silesia next, likely. Long disgraced, Fouche gets my secret call: entering Prussia, I set him over its rule. Lutzen drove them over the river. Come at once; the Regent alone knows.
tweets.nap-18130512-583: I delivered battle to the Russian and Prussian army, intrenched in the camps of Bautzen and of Kochkirch, on the and the. Providence granted me the victory. I hasten to inform your Majesty that my health is excellent, counting upon the interest you bear me.
tweets.nap-18130601-584: I have seen with pleasure that amidst the vicissitudes of political events the feelings of your Majesty have remained unchangeable. The evil intentions of Sweden towards me are the result of my constant refusal to adhere to the spoliation of Norway.
tweets.nap-18130602-585: You will see by the Moniteur that negotiations for an armistice are going on. It will probably be signed tomorrow or the day after. This armistice interferes with the course of my victories.
tweets.nap-18130607-586: I see with pleasure that my Son grows and continues to give hopes. I can but express my satisfaction for all the care you bestow upon him. The death of the due de Frioul pained me. This was the only time during twenty years that he did not guess what would please me.
tweets.nap-18130608-587: Play season sleeps; send at most six or seven picked players for as many pieces. No fuss, no roadside pomp. Yet let Paris buzz as if the whole tragedy sails, gossip serves me. Remusat chooses the troupe.
tweets.nap-18130630-588: Prince Metternich has handed me your Majesty's letter. I desire peace. If the Russians show themselves as moderate as I am it will be promptly concluded.
tweets.nap-18130701-589: Since war opened the allies never won so full a victory, against all our united strength, utterly overturning us. I record the disaster plainly; it shall be answered.
tweets.nap-18130717-590: I the Bishop of Nantes was the most enlightened priest of the empire, the most distinguished Doctor of the sorbonne; he can be placed alongside of the most honoured bishops of the gallican church.
tweets.nap-18130801-591: If I were at Paris, I should go to Cherbourg to be present at the introduction of the sea. I wish the Empress to go there, and, if she goes, it will be proper for you to accompany her. The marine might order something to do honour to the Empress and to amuse her.
tweets.nap-18130801-592: To Drouot: present my actors' bounty plan; Turenne ships the troupe home. To Cambaceres: see Savary, I gave him my view of things. Austria shall rue her folly and treason; I expect the truce denounced and her declaration within days.
tweets.nap-18130801-593: I the declaration of war on the part of Austria forebodes some big battles which will necessarily cost a large number of men. The unfortunate and unexpected turn which affairs have taken in Spain requires that the safety of the frontier should be guaranteed.
tweets.nap-18130807-594: Austria fields three hundred thousand: one hundred twenty thousand on Dresden, twenty thousand on Bavaria, fifty thousand on my viceroy. Oudinot, Vandamme, Regnier and Padoue debouch eighty thousand by Luckau and Bayreuth for Berlin.
tweets.nap-18130817-595: I have long thought that Caulaincourt and de Narbonne allow themselves to be taken in by the honeyed style of Metternich.
tweets.nap-18130826-596: I informed you of my intentions yesterday. The whole army of the enemy presented itself before Dresden yesterday, and Marshal St. Cyr feared that he would be attacked today; I am going there.
tweets.nap-18130901-598: Macdonald wavers at Gorlitz; must I ride to prop him? Vandamme's ruin beggars belief: no sentry, no reserve, yet the chief, they say, destroyed himself. His men pour back, generals and fifteen thousand with them; I count my loss a few thousand.
tweets.nap-18130902-599: Write thus to Marshal Ney: We have just received news from Marshal Oudinot who deemed fit to venture within two marches of Wittenberg.
tweets.nap-18130919-600: I general bruno was captured, not by 4,000, but by 400 men, while he was quietly sleeping in the town, with his whole force. As long as the light troops perform their duties so badly accidents will happen.
tweets.nap-18131007-601: I wrote to you this morning at one o'clock. I am starting for Meissen. The whole Silesian army has debouched by Wartenburg; there is no force from Dresden to Gorlitz, nor from Dresden to Berlin. Marshal St. Cyr will remain at Dresden.
tweets.nap-18131031-602: I have arrived here. The Bavarians and Austrians, 60,000 strong, posted at Hanau, tried to cut me off from France. I gave them a good drubbing, and captured their guns, standards, and 6,000 prisoners. My health was never better. I am going to Mayence.
tweets.nap-18131110-603: I am not aware if Belfort is in a state of defence. If so, have it armed, as well as all the castles along the Swiss frontier. Not that I have any reason to distrust the Swiss, but because in the present state of the empire it is necessary to arm on all sides.
tweets.nap-18131110-604: Give orders that if ever the English arrive at the castle of Marracq near Bayonne it be set fire to; also to all the houses which belong to me, so that they may not sleep in my bed.
tweets.nap-18131110-605: The movement of the English upon Bayonne has opened up a portion of the frontier. I learn that they have already landed a certain quantity of their merchandise near St. Jean-de-Luz. I suppose that you have removed your custom-house line. This matter deserves your attention.
tweets.nap-18140101-606: I consider it doubtful if the allies are acting in good faith, and if England desires peace. For myself I desire it, but solid and honourable. France without her natural limits, without Ostend and Antwerp, would not be on an equal footing with the other states of Europe.
tweets.nap-18140101-607: You will have seen, by the various documents which have been published, all the efforts made to obtain peace. I have since sent my Minister of Foreign affairs to the enemy's outposts. They put off receiving him and yet they march forward.
tweets.nap-18140110-609: I have had it placed in the orders of the palace that you shall henceforth be announced as King Joseph, and the queen as the Queen Julie, with all the honours, and in the manner usual with French princes.
tweets.nap-18140110-610: Bulow floods Belgium with twenty thousand, nine thousand of them Graham's English. Meet him with all you have. I trust your vigour where others temporize.
tweets.nap-18140116-611: PRINCE, The delays which have taken place in the negotiations are due neither to France nor to Austria, and yet France and Austria suffer the most from them. The allied armies have already invaded several of our provinces.
tweets.nap-18140201-612: Berthier sent you a courier from the field of battle. I have since despatched the young Montesquiou. It is 8 o'clock, and before going to sleep I send you two words to inform you that the affair of yesterday was decisive. The enemy's army of Silesia no longer exists.
tweets.nap-18140201-613: It is necessary that the vice-reine should go to Paris without delay in order to be confined, it being my intention that, under no circumstances, shall she remain in a country occupied by the enemy.
tweets.nap-18140201-614: What! Six hours after having received the first troops coming from Spain you were not in the field! Six hours' repose was sufficient. I won the action of Nangis with a brigade of dragoons coming from Spain, which, since it left Bayonne, had not unbridled its horses.
tweets.nap-18140201-615: I write to Marshal Soult that with his fine troops he ought to beat the Duke of Wellington, but that under present circumstances a little more decision and vigour are necessary.
tweets.nap-18140204-616: The report of Prince Schwartzenberg is a piece of folly. There has been no battle. The Old guard was not there; the Young guard was not engaged. A few guns were taken from us by charges of cavalry.
tweets.nap-18140206-617: I am much surprised that Marshal Suchet should not have despatched the troops which I demanded from Lyons. They ought to have arrived and I hear no more of them. If the marshal has taken upon himself not to execute orders he is very culpable.
tweets.nap-18140207-618: I see that instead of sustaining the Empress you discourage her. Why do you lose your head like that? What are these Misereres, and these prayers of forty hours at the chapel? Have people in Paris gone mad?
tweets.nap-18140207-619: I see with pleasure the advantages which you have obtained; if they had been a little more decisive we should have been able to keep Italy. I have destroyed the army of Silesia, composed of Russians and Prussians. I began yesterday to beat Schwartzenberg.
tweets.nap-18140210-620: I have just arrived at Nogent. The enemy after Montereau fell back upon Troyes with the greater portion of their army. They enjoyed great luck, for the frost enabled them to march across country; but for this half their baggage and their artillery would have been captured.
tweets.nap-18140214-621: I send you a line to let you know the happy issue of the battle of Vauchamps.
tweets.nap-18140301-623: I put the following note in the Moniteur: the Emperor had his head-quarters on the at berry-au-bac.
tweets.nap-18140301-624: Find Suchet's ten thousand; post five or six thousand to the Dordogne. I need my southern door barred.
tweets.nap-18140302-626: Write to Marshal Soult that with troops like his he should beat the enemy, if he will only exhibit pluck and place himself at the head of the troops. Let him understand that we have reached a period when more than ordinary resolution and vigour are required.
tweets.nap-18140303-627: Before commencing the fortifications of Paris the plan must be known; that which has been presented to me appears to be very complicated; more simplicity is required.
tweets.nap-18140310-628: The army which I beat at Craonne was the Russian army. It lost heavily, and fell back upon Laon, where it was joined by the corps of Bulow, York, and Kleist, forming the Prussian army.
tweets.nap-18140314-629: I have arrived at Rheims, which General St. Priest had occupied with three Russian divisions and a Prussian division which had just arrived from Stettin. I beat them; I retook the town, 20 guns, a great deal of baggage, and made 5,000 prisoners. General St.
tweets.nap-18140315-630: Marshal Mortier writes that the enemy are in full retreat, and seem to be falling back upon Laon. I have sent some cavalry to follow their march, which is being made in good order. Send some peasants to try and find out if the enemy are in force at Craonne.
tweets.nap-18140318-631: Write to Soissons to inform General Moreau, who commands there, that I have reached Fismes, and to tell him to send me news of Marshals Marmont and Mortier, who were to march upon Soissons. He must also tell me what he knows of the movements of the enemy.
tweets.nap-18140318-632: Yesterday I beat Winzingerode, Langeron, and Woronsow, united, with the remains of Sacken's army. I made 2,000 prisoners. The battle of Craonne is glorious. Marshals Victor and Grouchy were wounded. I have 700 or 800 killed or wounded.
tweets.nap-18140320-633: Yesterday I crossed the Aube at Plancy, and at once marched upon Mery. I attacked the town, which was carried by evening.
tweets.nap-18140323-634: I send disguised gendarmes to Metz, Bar and Nancy with my letters to the mayors.
tweets.nap-18140401-635: I have received your letter of the. Your conduct during recent times, when so many others behaved badly, has given me great pleasure. I thank you, and this confirms the opinion I had conceived of your character.
tweets.nap-18140408-636: I Send orders to Marshals Marmont, Mortier, Oudinot, and serrurier, and to generals Belliard, gerard, sorbier, Sebastiani, etc., to come to the palace this evening at ten o'clock, and to adopt measures so that they may be back at their posts before daybreak.
tweets.nap-18140610-637: It is my intention to appoint the mayor of Porto Longone commandant of my palace at Porto Longone. He must perform the functions of commandant, concierge, keeper of the robes, and overseer of the gardens. He will receive a salary of 600 francs.
tweets.nap-18140818-638: Colonel Laczinski, who is going to leave today for Leghorn, will go from there to Aix, and will take with him a letter from me to the Empress.
tweets.nap-18140826-639: I think that I asked you to write to the Princess Pauline not to bring her piano master with her, but only a good singer and a good songstress, seeing that we have here a good violin player and a good pianist.
tweets.nap-18150301-642: FRENCHMEN, The defection of Marshal Augereau delivered Lyons, without defence, to our enemies. The army which I confided to him was strong enough to beat the Austrians, and to fall upon the rear of the left wing of the army which threatened Paris.
tweets.nap-18150301-643: I have arrived. I have traversed France. The army and the people of country and of town came out to meet me. I entered Paris on the at the head of the camp of Essonne, upon which the king counted.
tweets.nap-18150410-644: You must efface Berthier, Marmont, Victor, Perignon, Augereau, and Kellermann from the list of marshals. You must present me a report, so that a pension may be granted to those marshals who have no fortune.
tweets.nap-18150426-645: Tell Marshal Suchet, if he is still at Lyons, to remain there, and if he has left send him a courier, so that he may return. I give the command of the army of the Alps definitively to that marshal.
tweets.nap-18150527-646: I it is probable that the guard will soon march; there will then remain no troops in Paris. It is important that by the, at the latest, the quartermaster-generals, colonels, majors, captains, etc., of the National guard should receive their commissions.
tweets.nap-18150601-647: Enclosed you will find a copy of the orders which I have given for the cavalry of the army. Marshal Grouchy will command it in chief. Give him a chief of the staff, and a general of artillery. All the generals on the unattached list are at his service.
tweets.nap-18150601-648: I Inform Marshal Suchet, by telegraph, that hostilities will open on the, and that he can seize upon montmelian on that day. If it be indispensable to do so before that date, owing to the movements of the enemy, he is authorised to act.
tweets.nap-18150601-649: I am going to transfer my Imperial head-quarters this evening to Beaumont. Tomorrow, the, I shall move to Charleroi, where the Prussian army is; this will give rise to a battle or to the retreat of the enemy.
tweets.nap-18150606-650: My dream is France as free as may be; I say may be, for anarchy always hatches absolute rule. Two hundred guns must crown the gates and works of Paris within days. Tell me when the first naval pieces arrive.
tweets.nap-18150616-651: I send you my aide-de-camp, General Flahault, with the present letter. I wish to write to you in detail because it is of the greatest importance. Marshal Grouchy is marching on Sombreffe with the third and fourth corps of infantry.
tweets.nap-17910123-01: From Bonifacio to Cape Corse, from Ajaccio to Bastia, nothing rises but a chorus of curses against you. Your friends hide, your kin disown you. You have ruined Corsica; you have sold its honour to the French.
tweets.nap-17931207-01: I have received all the various letters you wrote me. Here we are still much in the same pOSITION. The army is thirty thousand strong. We have eleven batteries against Fort Malbousquet. The siege continues as planned.
tweets.nap-17931224-02: I promised you brilliant successes, and you see I keep my word. Worn out with fatigue and work, I could not tell you first; suffice it that the English carried off none of our guns. The defence holds firm.
tweets.nap-17940104-01: Fort Saint-Nicolas cannot withstand a quarter-hour. The three walls closing it town-side are razed. I am pushing the works forward with all speed. The enemy will find no shelter there.
tweets.nap-17940228-03: More grain ships came into the roads this evening; but the enemy squadron keeps them from venturing through. I shall have two batteries built which, once finished, will make coastal traffic safe, under the very eyes of the enemy squadron.
tweets.nap-17940407-02: I order: Rebuild Sainte-Marguerite point battery; raise the mortar parapet eight feet. The works must be completed before the enemy can react. Speed is everything in these preparations.
tweets.nap-17940521-03: I say: Piedmont plain demands superior force; join the Alps and Italy armies for it. A divided command will fail; unity of effort is the only path to victory in that theatre.
tweets.nap-17940620-04: I set the plan: 1. Secure rearwards against enemies within and without. 2. Unite the Alps and Italy defence systems. 3. Concentrate artillery where it can strike the decisive blow. These are the pillars.
tweets.nap-17940627-05: Call it not Pelletier but Marguerite island; renaming places needs a Convention decree. I insist on the proper forms; revolutionary nomenclature must follow the law.
tweets.nap-17940702-06: The Republic breeds two alarmists: grain-famine criers and powder-fearers. Both spread panic to serve their own ends. I will not tolerate defeatism disguised as caution.
tweets.nap-17940702-07: It is imposture to claim 28 thousand powder at Antibes when you hold 45. I know the true state of the magazines; false returns will be punished severely.
tweets.nap-17940915-08: I wrote you several times unanswered; I cannot think it contempt. Perhaps my letters miscarried, but silence from a subordinate is not acceptable. Respond at once.
tweets.nap-17950601-33: I intend to use all haste with the commissions for your wife. Desiree demands my portrait; you will give it to her should she still wish for it; if not, keep it for yourself. Family matters must not distract from duty.
tweets.nap-17950618-09: Never take me for a dupe; these twenty days I know Saliceti hides with you. I see through the manoeuvres of those who think themselves clever. The truth will out.
tweets.nap-17950622-10: Your No. 16 received. Chiappe's letter pleased me. I shall do what I can for Lucien. Brother, your requests find a willing ear when they serve the cause.
tweets.nap-17950701-19: I am a general employed in the army of the West; my malady detains me here. I await further details from you. I believe you avoid speaking to me about Desiree on purpose.
tweets.nap-17950712-11: I say the English must re-embark within days. Pichegru prepares the Rhine crossing. The Vendée is quiet. The Chouans only north of the Loire. Peace with Spain is imminent.
tweets.nap-17950712-18: I report: English will re-embark in days. Pichegru prepares Rhine crossing. La Vendee tranquil, Chouans only north of Loire. Peace with Spain imminent. Dutch warm friends of Revolution. Italy grows rich on France spoils. Luxury and arts flourish astonishingly.
tweets.nap-17950724-12: I did not write, friend, for I had no pleasant news to give. Silence is sometimes the only honest report when affairs go ill.
tweets.nap-17950728-13: Twelve thousand émigrés landed at Quiberon, battering the isthmus passage. The Royalist invasion has begun; we must crush it before it spreads.
tweets.nap-17950817-20: I congratulate you on joining the army. Fortune, favour, esteem of men vary perpetually. I have been appointed general of the Line in La Vendee: I have not accepted. Many would command a brigade better; few command artillery so well.
tweets.nap-17950823-14: The Committee sent you, general, by last courier, Italy's direction instructions. You will execute them without delay. The army of Italy awaits your orders.
tweets.nap-17950825-04: I hope you will have a consulate in the kingdom of Naples, at peace with that power. All is very quiet here. A third of the Convention is about to be renewed. The political winds shift but we hold our course.
tweets.nap-17950830-15: We forward, general, a note just received from Switzerland. The diplomatic channels remain open; intelligence flows through them.
tweets.nap-17950905-16: The Committee thinks I cannot leave France while war lasts. They are right; my place is with the army, not in the chambers of politicians.
tweets.nap-17950906-21: No matter what, you need feel no alarm for me; I have friends among the best men of all parties. Mariette is zealous for me; you know his opinions. I am intimate with Doulcet. You know my friends of opposite opinion. I will write your wife.
tweets.nap-17950908-17: Yesterday I wrote her, friend; she will have it. Primary assemblies meet in three days. The electoral process moves forward despite the noise.
tweets.nap-17950912-18: Lest false rumors run at Genoa, I write you daily. Truth is the best antidote to the poison of speculation.
tweets.nap-17950915-19: I see the majority accepted constitution and renewal; Paris sections still ferment. The political settlement advances even as the streets murmur.
tweets.nap-17950923-05: We await the conclusion of Corsican affairs with some interest; here all is quiet. The Convention has the majority for the two-thirds. Within a month there will be no shock; the constitution will be established.
tweets.nap-17951011-20: The gazettes told you all: named second of the interior army. We conquered. Victory has its own voice; it needs no amplification.
tweets.nap-17951012-06: An essential error was committed in not forcing the entrenched camp of Ceva while the beaten Austrians were driven beyond Acqui. Our whole army stood available for that attack. The opportunity was lost through hesitation.
tweets.nap-17960311-01: I had Barras inform the Directory of my marriage to Citoyenne Tascher Beauharnais. The union is sealed; Josephine is now my wife.
tweets.nap-17960321-04: Your letter received. I dined today with General Schérer and your wife. Social ties bind the officer corps as much as duty.
tweets.nap-17960327-02: Soldiers, you are naked, ill-fed; the government owes you much and can give you nothing. But I will lead you to the most fertile plains in the world. There you will find honour, glory, and wealth.
tweets.nap-17960327-03: Enclosed the cavalry movement state; regiments arrive daily. The horse is the eye of the army; I will not be blind.
tweets.nap-17960328-05: Warmly received by the army, whose confidence obliges my liveliest gratitude. I will not betray the trust of men who follow me into fire.
tweets.nap-17960329-06: The 209th third battalion stands guilty of disobedience and mutiny. Discipline is the soul of armies; without it we are a mob. The ringleaders will answer for this.
tweets.nap-17960329-07: The cavalry divides in two divisions. I am arranging the horse for maximum effect on the coming march.
tweets.nap-17960329-08: I general parra will at once requisition antibes administrators. Supply must flow without delay.
tweets.nap-17960329-09: The General-in-Chief reviewed the 100th and 165th demi-brigades. Their bearing pleases me; they will do their duty.
tweets.nap-17960331-10: I want the staff roll tonight of every officer marching. The command must be complete before we move.
tweets.nap-17960331-11: I adjutant-general chabran leaves Nice today for Albenga post-haste. Speed in transmission is everything.
tweets.nap-17960402-01: I have learned with pain that our troops allowed themselves to be surprised yesterday at the village of St. Michel. By these various movements you will be in a pOSITION to take your revenge in a brilliant fashion.
tweets.nap-17960403-12: The General-in-Chief renews orders to hasten the new organisation. Disorder is the enemy of victory; I will have order.
tweets.nap-17960404-13: I a 400-sack contribution levied on oneille valley. The army feeds itself from the land it conquers.
tweets.nap-17960405-14: I convene a Nice military commission for émigré moulin, taken at Ormea. Traitors face military justice.
tweets.nap-17960406-02: I have transferred my head-quarters to Albenga. The movement against Genoa drew the enemy from winter quarters. Beaulieu published a manifesto; I shall reply after the battle.
tweets.nap-17960406-15: I raise a laigueglia-pietra brigade for carts, forage, hospitals. Logistics win campaigns.
tweets.nap-17960406-16: I reviewed the and with published satisfaction. Good troops deserve recognition.
tweets.nap-17960407-17: I levy two hundred mules at pieve, Ormea and garessio for food. The army moves on its stomach.
tweets.nap-17960408-18: Sir, an émigré is a parricidal son no rank can sanctify; yours dishonour your army. I will not treat with traitors.
tweets.nap-17960410-19: I learn Genoa molests patriots and troubles France's friends. The Republic protects its own wherever they are.
tweets.nap-17960411-20: Hold your troops ready to march at first signal, food issued; I want them ready.
tweets.nap-17960411-21: I Augereau marches two demi-brigades and four squadrons to mallare. The offensive begins now.
tweets.nap-17960411-22: I finale's artillery marches with 8-pounder, 4s, howitzer and all munitions. Guns follow the bayonet.
tweets.nap-17960414-03: The Italian campaign has commenced. I have forwarded a report on the battle of Montenotte. After manoeuvring three days to conceal his intentions, Beaulieu attacked the right of our army with 10,000 men.
